title: What happens when a browser loads a page
purpose: Follow one page load through DNS, TCP, TLS, the HTTP request and the response, in order.
sequence_reason: Each step can start only after the step before it finishes, so the order of events is the idea.
summary: The browser asks DNS for the server address, opens a TCP connection with a three-way handshake, agrees on encryption keys with TLS, sends a GET request and receives a 200 OK response with the HTML, then requests the files the page needs.
explanation: A page load is a chain: name lookup, connection, encryption, request and response. A slow early step delays every later step.

learning_check.question: Why can the browser not send the GET request before the TCP handshake finishes?
learning_check.answer: The request travels over the TCP connection, and with HTTPS the TLS handshake must also finish first, so there is no channel to send it on yet.

scenes.heading: One page load, five steps
scenes.narration: Loading a page takes five steps, and each one waits for the step before it.

scenes.heading: Find the server address
scenes.narration: First, the browser asks a DNS resolver for the IP address of the server name.

path.label: The browser asks for the address
The resolver answers with the IP address

scenes.heading: Open a TCP connection
scenes.narration: Next, the browser and the server do the TCP handshake: SYN, then SYN-ACK, then ACK.

scenes.heading: Agree on encryption with TLS
scenes.narration: For HTTPS, a TLS handshake follows. The server sends its certificate, and both sides agree on keys.

items: ClientHello: the browser proposes keys and ciphers
ServerHello and certificate: the server proves its name
Keys agreed: from now on, traffic is encrypted

scenes.heading: Send the request, get the response
scenes.narration: Now the browser sends a GET request. The server answers with a status line, 200 OK, and the HTML.

path.label: The status code says the request succeeded

scenes.heading: Fetch the rest, then render
scenes.narration: The browser reads the HTML, requests the CSS, scripts and images it names, and renders the page.

items: Request CSS, scripts and images, often on the same connection
